title: Stabilizer criterion for membership in the DM locus
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, and $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal X$ its largest open substack with unramified relative diagonal. Let $K$ be any field and $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$ an $S$-morphism. Let $G_x$ be the automorphism group algebraic space of the object $x$, namely the sheaf $T\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X(T)}(x_T)$ on $K$-schemes. Then $x$ factors through $\mathcal U$ if and only if $G_x\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is unramified. No perfectness assumption on $K$ is imposed. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids on schemes with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and scheme atlases use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and smooth means [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Open substacks are full substacks whose pullback by every scheme is an open subscheme. A representable morphism is unramified if every scheme base change, on etale scheme charts of its algebraic-space source, is unramified in [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0DSN (lemma-points-DM-locus), part (1); relative-base convention via Tag 050N (lemma-separated-implies-morphism-separated), part (1).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:P\to\mathcal X$ and write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal X,P}(p)$. By [lem-sfb-stack-isom-space-locally-finite-type], $G$ is an algebraic space locally of finite type over $P$. Composition, identity and inversion of automorphisms make it a group algebraic space. On $R=P\times_{\mathcal X}P$, the defining isomorphism $\alpha:p s\xrightarrow{\sim}p t$ identifies $s^*G$ with $t^*G$ by $g\mapsto\alpha g\alpha^{-1}$; its inverse is conjugation by $\alpha^{-1}$. These formulas commute with pullback because composition and inversion do.

source.place: Tag 0DSN, proof: choose a smooth atlas and its automorphism group; Tag 04XR supplies local finite type.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-base-locus] to $G\to P$ and denote its maximal open by $V\subseteq P$. By its arbitrary base-change clause, $s^{-1}V$ and $t^{-1}V$ are the maximal unramified base loci of $s^*G$ and $t^*G$, respectively. The conjugation isomorphism of step 1 preserves unramifiedness and open containment, so these two maximal opens are equal. Thus $V$ is invariant under the presentation groupoid.

source.place: Tag 0DSN, proof: construction of the maximal atlas open and equality of its two pullbacks; Tag 0DSJ (1).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], $V$ descends to an open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$ with $P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal W=V$. The restriction $V\to\mathcal W$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas: its scheme pullbacks are precisely the atlas pullbacks of $P\to\mathcal X$. Its automorphism algebraic space is $G\times_P V$, since $\mathcal W$ is full. Step 2 makes this group unramified over $V$, so [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-automorphism-diagonal-test] applied to $V\to\mathcal W$ says that $\Delta_{\mathcal W/S}$ is unramified. Hence maximality of the open $\mathcal U$ in the statement gives $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 0DSN, proof: descend the invariant open using Tag 0507, then apply the inertia/diagonal criterion Tag 0CL0 (4).

proof.text: Conversely let $P_{\mathcal U}=P\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$, an open subscheme of $P$ and a smooth surjective atlas of $\mathcal U$. Its automorphism space is $G\times_P P_{\mathcal U}$, again by fullness. Since $\Delta_{\mathcal U/S}$ is unramified, [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-automorphism-diagonal-test] makes this group unramified over $P_{\mathcal U}$. Maximality in [lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-base-locus] implies $P_{\mathcal U}\subseteq V$. The inclusion-preserving bijection of [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] therefore gives $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal W$. Together with step 3 this identifies $\mathcal W=\mathcal U$ and $P_{\mathcal U}=V$.

source.place: Tag 0DSN, proof: identify the constructed open with the largest DM open.

proof.text: For the given $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$, put $Q=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{\mathcal X}P$, with maps $a:Q\to P$ and $b:Q\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. This is an algebraic space smooth and surjective over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ by [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], hence is nonempty. By [lem-sfb-stack-isom-space-locally-finite-type], $G_x$ is locally of finite type over $K$, so [lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-base-locus] gives its maximal unramified base open $V_x\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}K$. The tautological isomorphism $p a\simeq x b$ identifies $a^*G$ with $b^*G_x$ by conjugation, as in step 1. The base-change clause of the same group-locus lemma therefore identifies $a^{-1}V=b^{-1}V_x$ in $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0DSN, proof: comparison of the automorphism groups after atlas pullback; Tag 0DSJ (1), applied to both maps from Q.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent] and step 4, $x$ factors through $\mathcal U$ exactly when $a:Q\to P$ factors through $V$, equivalently when $a^{-1}V=Q$. Step 5 replaces the latter equality by $b^{-1}V_x=Q$. The spectrum of a field has a single point, so its only opens are empty and the whole spectrum; since $Q$ is nonempty, this equality is equivalent to $V_x=\operatorname{Spec}K$. By the defining maximality and unramifiedness clauses of [lem-sfb-group-space-unramified-base-locus], $V_x=\operatorname{Spec}K$ is equivalent to $G_x\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ being unramified. This proves both directions for the original field $K$.

source.place: Tag 0DSN (1): conclude the point test from arbitrary base change of the group locus; the two-open observation is elementary.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0DSN (lemma-points-DM-locus), proof of (1), obtained from its written proof of (2) by using unramifiedness. The final field test uses the entire pulled-back atlas instead of choosing a field extension.
